failures.triage_note: PARTIAL FIX since the prior run. The dangerous half is fixed: the prior run found Save actually persisted an empty title (real data loss on media_id 125). This run confirms the server now correctly refuses -- PUT /mvs/v1/media/64 with title:'' returns HTTP 400 rest_invalid_param, and the stored title (media_id=64, 'Alpine Mountain Sunrise') is unchanged in the DB after the attempt. But the UI half the task asked to re-verify ('Save DISABLED' while title is empty) was never wired: Save's disabled binding is data-wp-bind--disabled="state.editModal.saving" only, no title-empty condition. Clicking Save with a blank title now silently no-ops client-side (no PUT fires, no visible error -- an empty error slot exists in the DOM but is never populated), violating the runbook's 'no silent action' gate. Net: no data can be lost anymore, but the exact UI contract this retest was asked to confirm does not pass.
failures.expected: Owner opens Edit Media modal on /my-media/, clears Title -> Save button becomes disabled immediately. If a save is attempted anyway, a visible error appears and the server refuses with 400.
failures.actual: Save button stays enabled (disabled=false) after the Title field is cleared to ''. Clicking it does not send a PUT request and shows no visible error message. Direct REST call to PUT /mvs/v1/media/64 with title:'' correctly returns HTTP 400 rest_invalid_param, and the DB title is unchanged -- server-side data protection now works, client-side gating/feedback still does not.

failures.triage_note: Root cause is in Free's own code, not simply Pro's absence: MediaUrl::variant_url() (includes/Core/MediaUrl.php) resolves a variant through StorageService::get_driver_for_location(), whose final fallback is get_driver() -> apply_filters('mvs_storage_driver', null, $name) -> LocalDriver when nothing hooks the filter. Only Pro's driver classes (S3/BunnyCDN/R2/DOSpaces) hook that filter, so in free-only mode every cloud-hosted variant resolves through LocalDriver, which always returns a non-empty local URL -- so variant_url() never reaches its documented fallback to the correct legacy CDN meta value. The code's own doc-comment warns this exact host-mismatch class 403'd WebP behind a CDN before (Basecamp #10162798416); this reproduces the same class, just not yet 404ing because local mirror copies still exist.
failures.expected: On the per-media Details view for media_id=64 (the item migrated to BunnyCDN), the 'Open the original image', 'Open WebP copy', and all three per-size 'View ->' links (Large/Medium/Thumbnail) should all resolve on mediaverse1.b-cdn.net, matching the stored file_url/thumb_* meta, and none should 404.
failures.actual: Only 'Open the original image' correctly points at https://mediaverse1.b-cdn.net/wpmediaverse/2026/08/1e602735c00b673e.jpg. 'Open WebP copy' and all 3 'View ->' size links instead point at http://mediaverse.local/wp-content/uploads/wpmediaverse/2026/08/1e602735c00b673e*.{jpg,webp} -- a different host than the primary link for the same media item. curl confirms both hosts currently return HTTP 200 for every one of these URLs (local mirrors have not been cleaned up), so nothing visibly 404s today, but the page is silently serving 5 of 6 links from the wrong location for a cloud-migrated item, and will 404 once local cleanup runs.

failures.triage_note: Reproduced on a completely unrelated stock WordPress Page with zero plugin markup (/sample-page/?s=test also 404s), and no new debug.log entries appear when it happens -- confirms this is WordPress core / rewrite-permalink query-var routing on this site short-circuiting BEFORE wpmediaverse's own explore.php template (which correctly reads $_GET['s'] and implements the documented friendly empty state) ever executes. wpmediaverse's own template code for this contract is correct; the site's routing is swallowing the request first. Still filed because it fully blocks a documented customer contract on this install, but the fix is not a wpmediaverse code change.
failures.expected: /explore-media/?s=zzznoresults999 renders the Explore page with a 'no results for {term}' heading, a 'Browse all media' link, and >=5 popular-tag chips.
failures.actual: /explore-media/?s=zzznoresults999 (and any other search term, e.g. ?s=mountain) returns a hard HTTP 404 'Page not found' -- worse than the originally described regression (a generic empty state); the page does not render at all.
